title: app nav: a per-audience landing (and group placement) cannot name an entry contributed by a module package — so an industry module can never be a role's landing page or reorder past the app's own groups
body:
Found by a downstream app on the published 18.4.0 packages (steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#70: reorganising one CRM app's navigation around an industry module, measured per role on 10 accounts).

## Limits hit

1. An app's landing item may name only the app's **own** navigation entries. An entry contributed by a module package through `navigationContributions` (e.g. the industry module's Sales Order list, its Master Data group, or a service module's Service Overview) can never be a per-audience landing. Consequence downstream: a sales rep cannot land on the module's Sales Orders; the system officer cannot land on Master Data; and the app must keep the Service group ahead of Customers / Sales only because the service staff's landing (Service Overview, a contributed entry) is reached by ordering, not by a landing key.
2. A contribution is appended after the target group's own items (`applyNavContributions`, by group id + priority): a module cannot place its entry between two of the app's entries (e.g. Sales Order next to Opportunities), and cannot declare a group in the app — the app must pre-declare every group a module may fill.

## Why it matters

Industry modules (the intended way to extend a packaged CRM per customer) cannot shape the daily entry point of the roles they exist for; apps end up editing the upstream app's navigation to make room, which every upstream sync must replay.

## Suggested fix shape (for the lane to judge)

Let a landing name any entry present in the merged navigation (own or contributed), validated after contributions are applied; and let a contribution declare a position relative to an app entry (`before` / `after` an id) within the bounds the app allows.

Dedupe words: landing contributed entry · navigationContributions position · module landing page · nav contribution before after.
